tools.falsifier: REFUTED IF: settings are written with NO confirm card (Tier A), OR the model sends a `model_source`/`model_ref` the author never mentioned — three fields, one named — OR a target_language outside the declared enum. A run ending in a provider stream error is evidence about the TRANSPORT and a re-run condition, never about this tool.

ship_audit.gate: NOT REACHED — the tool was never called on a completing turn. On the rail-pinned phrasing the turn never emits an assistant message at all.
ship_audit.absent_case: EXERCISED by direct probe — another owner's book is refused 'not found or not accessible'.
ship_audit.empty_case: OWED — a call with no field to change was never exercised through the tool.
ship_audit.tenancy: EXERCISED by direct probe — refused with the same wording an absent id gets, so it is no existence oracle.

tools.blocked_reason:
BLOCKED — and after SEVEN arms of calling it 'transport errors', the cause is now diagnosed and it was never the transport.

WHAT SEVEN ARMS LOOKED LIKE: surfaced 5/5 every time, and 5, 1, 4, 4, 5, 5 then 4 of 5 runs ending in "upstream sent 'error' with no error message (response id '', status '')". I recorded that as a provider fault and as a tool that 'cannot be measured on this turn shape'. That was a description of the symptom, not a diagnosis, and it was wrong about the cause.

WHAT THE SERVER LOG SAYS, for this exact prompt:
    intent pinned workflow(s) ['translation-pass'] from the user's request
    rail translation-pass: 0/3 steps done, next=translation_coverage
    rail vision-to-book: 0/9 steps done, next=glossary_list_system_standards
    interrupt-persist detached ... (write continues after cancel)
    CP-0.4 orphaned turn: no assistant row, outcome 'abandoned_by_user' stamped

The request PINS A RAIL. The server drives the rail's steps and the turn NEVER EMITS AN ASSISTANT MESSAGE — no assistant row is ever written. The client waits until its budget runs out and reports whatever it has, which is an empty upstream error.

🔴 THE TIMEOUT WAS NOT THE CAUSE EITHER, WHICH IS WHY THE CONTROL MATTERED. The harness's turn budget was a hard-coded 180s, so the obvious story was 'a rail is slow and the client gives up'. Raising it to 900s changed the error from STREAM_ERROR to ReadTimeout and nothing else: the turn still never completed. Slowness would have been fixed by more time. This is not slowness.

THE CONTROL THAT PROVED IT. Same tool, same fixture, same batch machinery — the ONLY change is phrasing that does not pin the rail, and still from this tool's own declared synonyms ('change model' / 'update settings' instead of 'set target language ... translation'):
    'Set the target language for this book's translation to Vietnamese.'  -> turn never completes
    'Change this book's translation model to my default one.'            -> 5/5 CLEAN, 0 errors
A rail-pinned turn hangs; the same request phrased past the rail completes normally.

NAMING IT: D-RAIL-PINNED-TURN-NEVER-COMPLETES. It is worth an owner's attention beyond this tool, because the words that pin the rail are ordinary ones an author would use — and the failure is not a visible error to them, it is a chat turn that simply never answers.

THE TOOL ITSELF remains unproven: it was never called on a clean turn, so there is no evidence about it. That is what `blocked` means here, and it is concluded from the CLEAN control arm (0 errors) rather than from any of the seven dirty ones.
